newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil removes low-tariff status for 21 imports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil removes low-tariff status for 21 imports.

text.p: Brazil has removed 19 types of paper products and two categories of chemicals from a low-tariff group of import items, a government official said.
The decision effectively increases to between 12 and 16 percent from 4-6 percent import tariffs on the items, said the official who asked not to be named.
The chemicals affected are caustic soda and vynil acetate.
In May last year, the government included the 21 items among 300 types of imports which Brazil may import under a special, lower tariff under the terms of the Mercosur trade agreement.
The official said the items were originally included on the list because of high internatonal prices at the time which have since fallen, reducing the need for their inclusion.
Brazil recently increased import tariffs on a range of goods, including toys and pencils, and set restrictive quotas on textile imports.
It is also facing consultations at the World Trade Organization over a regime linking auto import tariffs to local manufacturing presence.
